High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Court No. - 84
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 4968 of 2023
Applicant :- Smt. Bachchi Devi

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Rajesh Kumar Sharma,Abhas Sharma

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Dasarathi Das,Madan Ji Pandey,Sudhir Kumar Agarwal
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. This application has been moved on behalf of the applicant Smt. Bachchi Devi seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 311of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station- Tharvai, District- Prayagraj.

3. It is alleged in the FIR that the marriage of the deceased, daughter of the informant was solemnized with co-accused Shekhar Yadav on 15.5.2022 and she was being subjected to cruelty and harassment for demand of additional dowry.
The informant was informed about all the incidents by the deceased herself.
Subsequently dowry death was caused by the in-laws of the deceased.
FIR was lodged and investigation started, which is continued.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and has no concern with the present matter.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.

It is further submitted that the accused applicant is a very old lady and heart patient and her treatment is going Smt. Bachchi Devi vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160781312/
1 on.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the ertiga car which was allegedly given in dowry by the informant was in fact purchased by the co-accused Shekhar Yadav, husband of the deceased, through bank finance and the loan installments are being paid by him to the bank.
It is further submitted that the co-accused Suresh Chand Yadav, husband of the present applicant and father-in-law of the deceased was refused bail and ultimately he died in jail.

It is further submitted that the deceased did not want to live with her husband on account of his being less educated and was insisting to live separately,
ultimately she committed suicide.
Investigation is going on and the accused applicant is cooperating with the I.O. of the case.
It has been submitted that in case applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.

5. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant vehemently opposing the bail application submit that it is a case of dowry death and ample evidence has been collected during the course of investigation against the accused applicant.
It is further submitted that only within six months of marriage the deceased died otherwise than under normal circumstances.
The ertiga car was purchased with the money given by the informant in the marriage.
Hence, the applicant is not entitled for any assistance by this Court.

6. In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has settled held that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, llikelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences,
the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

7. Hence, considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion of the merits of the case, I deem it not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the present applicant.
Such a person, who does not cooperate in the matter, is not entitled for any relief from this Court by way of granting anticipatory bail.
Prayer made in the application is refused.
8. The anticipatory bail application is rejected.
